## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity

## plugin:bio-research:chembl

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.

drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:

• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"

• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"


## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.

61	impl Scenario {
62	    /// Every scenario, in table order.
63	    pub const ALL: &'static [Scenario] = &[
64	        Scenario::CleanStop,
65	        Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason,
66	        Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration,
67	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration,
68	        Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason,
69	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration,
70	        Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason,
71	        Scenario::FragmentedToolName,
72	        Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop,
73	        Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop,
74	    ];
75	
76	    /// Whether this scenario's script must let the translator observe a stop
77	    /// reason. Cross-checked against each subject's own declaration so a
78	    /// mis-transcribed fixture cannot make assertion 3 pass vacuously.
79	    pub fn expects_stop_reason(self) -> bool {
80	        matches!(
81	            self,
82	            Scenario::CleanStop
83	                | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason
84	                | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
85	                | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
86	                | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
87	                | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
88	        )
89	    }
90	}
91	
92	/// A contract violation, classified. Ordering matters — see `classify`.
93	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
94	pub enum Violation {
95	    /// More than one `Finish` was emitted (assertion 1).
96	    DuplicateFinish,
97	    /// A `Usage` was emitted after `Finish` (assertion 2).
98	    UsageAfterFinish,
99	    /// Any other event, or an `Err`, was emitted after `Finish` (assertion 1).
100	    EventAfterFinish,
101	    /// End-of-stream after an observed stop reason emitted no `Finish`
102	    /// (assertion 3).
103	    MissingFinish,
104	    /// A `Finish` was emitted although no stop reason was observed
105	    /// (assertion 4).
106	    FinishOnTruncation,
107	    /// A `Finish` was emitted after cancellation (assertion 5).
108	    FinishOnCancel,
109	    /// A `Finish` was emitted after a mid-stream error (assertion 6).
110	    FinishAfterError,
111	    /// A `call_id` carried a number of name-bearing deltas other than one, or
112	    /// the name did not match the fixture's declared tool name (assertion 7).
113	    ToolNameNotExactlyOnce {
114	        /// The call whose name emission was wrong.
115	        call_id: String,
116	        /// How many deltas for that `call_id` carried `Some(name)`.
117	        count: usize,
118	    },
119	    /// A `ProviderData` event named a `call_id` for which the stream carried no
120	    /// `ToolCallDelta` (assertion 8).
121	    ProviderDataUnknownCall {
122	        /// The `call_id` that no streamed tool call used.
123	        call_id: String,
124	    },
125	    /// The stream did not produce the minimum evidence its scenario requires,
126	    /// so the assertions would have passed vacuously.
127	    InsufficientEvidence(&'static str),
128	    /// The terminal event carried a different `FinishReason` than the
129	    /// subject's fixture declares, so the bytes served are not the ones the
130	    /// scenario describes (spec §7.1).
131	    FinishReasonMismatch {
132	        /// What the subject's `fixture_finish_reason` declared.
133	        expected: FinishReason,
134	        /// What the stream actually emitted.
135	        observed: FinishReason,
136	    },
137	    /// The stream did not terminate within the per-scenario timeout.
138	    Timeout,
139	    /// The subject's `encodes_stop_reason` disagreed with the scenario's own
140	    /// expectation, so its fixture does not match the script it claims.
141	    StopReasonDeclarationMismatch {
142	        /// What the scenario requires.
143	        expected: bool,
144	        /// What the subject declared.
145	        declared: bool,
146	    },
147	}
148	
149	/// Released by the harness once it has observed the gate event, letting the
150	/// server send the remaining chunks.
151	pub struct GateHandle {
152	    /// Signalled by the harness; the server waits on the paired receiver.
153	    /// Named `tx` rather than `release` so it does not shadow the method below.
154	    pub(crate) tx: tokio::sync::oneshot::Sender<()>,
155	}
156	
157	impl GateHandle {
158	    /// Let the server send the remaining chunks.
159	    ///
160	    /// Returns whether the server was still parked on this gate. `false` means
161	    /// it had already run its script to the end, so nothing was being withheld
162	    /// — which is how a cancellation scenario silently degrades into an ungated
163	    /// one, and why `assert_conforms` reads this value rather than discarding
164	    /// it.
165	    pub fn release(self) -> bool {
166	        self.tx.send(()).is_ok()
167	    }
168	}
169	
170	/// What a subject did with a scenario.
171	///
172	/// Declining is a first-class outcome carrying a mandatory reason, not an
173	/// `Option` a caller can silently treat as a skip.
174	pub enum Outcome {
175	    /// The subject served the scenario.
176	    Served {
177	        /// The stream returned by the subject's `Model::invoke`.
178	        stream: BoxStream<'static, Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
179	        /// Present only for the cancellation scenarios.
180	        gate: Option<GateHandle>,
181	    },
182	    /// The wire shape cannot physically occur for this provider. The reason is
183	    /// printed in the report and must match the pinned decline set.
184	    Declined(&'static str),
185	}
186	
187	/// One provider backend under test.
188	#[async_trait::async_trait]
189	pub trait StreamUnderTest {
190	    /// Stable subject name, e.g. `"openai/chat"`. Used in failure output and to
191	    /// match rows in the pinned decline set.
192	    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
193	
194	    /// Whether this subject's fixture for `scenario` encodes a stop reason.
195	    /// Cross-checked against the scenario's own expectation.
196	    fn encodes_stop_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> bool;
197	
198	    /// The tool name this subject's tool-call fixtures declare.
199	    fn fixture_tool_name(&self) -> &'static str;
200	
201	    /// The `FinishReason` this subject's fixture for `scenario` declares, or
202	    /// `None` for scenarios that must not produce a `Finish` at all.
203	    ///
204	    /// Exactly four scenarios end with a `Finish`, and the floor checks this
205	    /// value for all four: `CleanStop`, `ToolCallCleanStop`,
206	    /// `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`, and `TruncatedAfterStopReason`, where
207	    /// assertion 3 requires the buffered stop reason to be flushed at
208	    /// end-of-stream. Every other scenario must return
209	    /// `None` — a cancelled or errored stream withholds `Finish`, and a
210	    /// truncation with no stop reason observed never had one to emit.
211	    ///
212	    /// The four differ in one way only: for the three clean stops a missing
213	    /// `Finish` fails the floor, whereas for `TruncatedAfterStopReason` it is
214	    /// `classify`'s `MissingFinish` (the SMA-531 shape). Either way, a `Finish`
215	    /// that *is* emitted must carry what this method declares.
216	    ///
217	    /// Declared per subject rather than inferred suite-side because only the
218	    /// fixture knows what its bytes encode: a checker that assumed
219	    /// `CleanStop` ⇒ `Stop` would silently accept a fixture that had been
220	    /// transcribed with the wrong stop reason.
221	    fn fixture_finish_reason(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<FinishReason>;
222	
223	    /// Serve `scenario` and return the subject's `Model::invoke` stream.
224	    async fn stream(&self, scenario: Scenario, cancel: CancellationToken) -> Outcome;
225	}
226	
227	/// How long one scenario's drain may run before the suite gives up on it.
228	///
229	/// A subject whose stream never terminates is a real bug this suite should
230	/// catch, and without a bound it would hang `cargo test` rather than fail it.
231	/// Generous on purpose: it is only ever reached on failure, so it costs nothing
232	/// on a green run.
233	const DRAIN_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
234	
235	/// How long a gated stream must stay silent before the harness accepts that the
236	/// server is parked on the gate and fires cancellation.
237	///
238	/// **Why quiescence and not a named gate edge.** The design spec's §6.1 has the
239	/// harness block on a specific event — a `TokenDelta` for `CancelMidGeneration`,
240	/// the `Usage` the fixture places after the stop-reason chunk for
241	/// `CancelAfterStopReason`. That does not survive contact with Anthropic, which
242	/// emits a `Usage` from `message_start` (`anthropic/stream.rs:79`): "cancel on
243	/// the first `Usage`" would fire before any stop reason was buffered, and
244	/// `CancelAfterStopReason` would silently degrade into `CancelMidGeneration` for
245	/// that subject. Silence is subject-independent, and — unlike an event
246	/// predicate — is itself positive evidence that the server is withholding.
247	///
248	/// **What a slow machine does to it.** Firing *late* (the harness task is
249	/// descheduled, so the window elapses later in wall-clock terms) is harmless:
250	/// the server is parked either way and nothing else is in flight. Firing
251	/// *early* is the dangerous direction, and the timer arms twice with different
252	/// stakes:
253	///
254	/// - **Between two events.** Needs two consecutive pre-gate chunks more than
255	///   this far apart, which the server does not produce: `feed` pushes every
256	///   pre-gate chunk into an unbounded channel with no await between them, so
257	///   they reach the socket back-to-back over loopback. If it ever did happen,
258	///   the consequence is a weaker test — cancellation at an earlier truncation
259	///   point — not a red run.
260	/// - **Before the first event**, which is the arming that can actually fail a
261	///   run. It covers connect, request, response head and first chunk, with
262	///   nothing yet consumed. Should *that* window elapse, the token fires having
263	///   collected nothing and the scenario dies on the "no TokenDelta" floor — a
264	///   spurious failure, not a weaker test. Sub-millisecond on loopback, but it
265	///   is the first thing to suspect behind an intermittent cancel-scenario
266	///   failure, ahead of anything in the provider.
267	///
268	/// The `server_was_parked` evidence below is unaffected in every case.
269	const GATE_QUIESCENCE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(400);
270	
271	/// Run every [`Scenario`] against `subject` and panic on the first thing that
272	/// does not hold.
273	///
274	/// Three guards run in order for each served scenario, and each exists because
275	/// of a specific way this suite could go quietly useless:
276	///
277	/// 1. **The stop-reason declaration is cross-checked.** Assertions 3 and 4 are
278	///    conditioned on whether a stop reason was observed, and that cannot be
279	///    inferred from the emitted events — a provider wrongly suppressing
280	///    `Finish` looks identical to one that correctly never saw a stop reason.
281	/// 2. **The positive-evidence floors run before the assertions.** A stream that
282	///    emits nothing satisfies "ends with `Finish`" trivially, so a miswired
283	///    adapter serving the wrong fixture would otherwise pass every assertion by
284	///    producing nothing at all.
285	/// 3. **Then, and only then, the events are classified** by the crate's
286	///    `classify` function.
287	///
288	/// Afterwards the observed declines are compared against the pinned
289	/// [`DECLINED`] table in both directions.
290	pub async fn assert_conforms(subject: &impl StreamUnderTest) {
291	    let name = subject.name();
292	    let mut declined: Vec<(Scenario, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
293	
294	    for &scenario in Scenario::ALL {
295	        let cancel = CancellationToken::new();
296	        let (stream, gate) = match subject.stream(scenario, cancel.clone()).await {
297	            Outcome::Declined(reason) => {
298	                declined.push((scenario, reason));
299	                continue;
300	            }
301	            Outcome::Served { stream, gate } => (stream, gate),
302	        };
303	
304	        let declared = subject.encodes_stop_reason(scenario);
305	        let expected = scenario.expects_stop_reason();
306	        if declared != expected {
307	            fail(
308	                name,
309	                scenario,
310	                &Violation::StopReasonDeclarationMismatch { expected, declared },
311	                "the subject's fixture does not encode what this scenario requires, so \
312	                 assertions 3 and 4 would be checked against the wrong condition",
313	            );
314	        }
315	
316	        let cancelled = is_cancel_scenario(scenario);
317	        if cancelled && gate.is_none() {
318	            fail(
319	                name,
320	                scenario,
321	                &Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
322	                    "a cancellation scenario was served without a gate, so the whole body was \
323	                     already on its way and cancellation could not truncate anything",
324	                ),
325	                "give the script a `gate_after` and hand the `GateHandle` back in \
326	                 `Outcome::Served`",
327	            );
328	        }
329	
330	        let Ok(drained) =
331	            tokio::time::timeout(DRAIN_TIMEOUT, drain(stream, gate, scenario, cancel)).await
332	        else {
333	            fail(
334	                name,
335	                scenario,
336	                &Violation::Timeout,
337	                "the stream never ended. For a cancellation scenario, check that the driver \
338	                 selects on the cancellation token while awaiting the next chunk; otherwise \
339	                 check that the script's ending actually closes the body",
340	            );
341	        };
342	
343	        if let Some(violation) = floor_violation(
344	            scenario,
345	            &drained.events,
346	            subject.fixture_tool_name(),
347	            subject.fixture_finish_reason(scenario),
348	        ) {
349	            fail(
350	                name,
351	                scenario,
352	                &violation,
353	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
354	            );
355	        }
356	
357	        if let Some(violation) = drained.cancel_violation() {
358	            fail(
359	                name,
360	                scenario,
361	                &violation,
362	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
363	            );
364	        }
365	
366	        if let Some(violation) = classify(&drained.events, scenario, cancelled) {
367	            fail(
368	                name,
369	                scenario,
370	                &violation,
371	                &format!("observed: {}", summarise(&drained.events)),
372	            );
373	        }
374	    }
375	
376	    assert_declines_match(name, &declined);
377	}

379	/// Whether `scenario` cancels the stream part-way through.
380	fn is_cancel_scenario(scenario: Scenario) -> bool {
381	    matches!(
382	        scenario,
383	        Scenario::CancelMidGeneration | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason
384	    )
385	}
386	
387	/// Everything one scenario's drain observed.
388	struct Drained {
389	    /// The events the subject's stream produced, in order.
390	    events: Vec<Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
391	    /// Present only for a cancellation scenario.
392	    cancel: Option<CancelEvidence>,
393	}
394	
395	/// Proof that a cancellation scenario actually cancelled something.
396	///
397	/// Dropping a [`GateHandle`] releases the body, so a cancellation scenario can
398	/// silently degrade into an ungated one — the whole script plays out, the
399	/// stream ends on its own, and the assertions pass without cancellation ever
400	/// having been exercised. Both fields below are recorded so that degradation
401	/// fails loudly instead.
402	struct CancelEvidence {
403	    /// The stream fell quiet, so the harness fired the cancellation token.
404	    /// `false` means the stream ended by itself first.
405	    fired: bool,
406	    /// The server was still parked on the gate when the stream ended, so the
407	    /// rest of the script was never delivered.
408	    server_was_parked: bool,
409	}
410	
411	impl Drained {
412	    /// The missing-evidence violation for a cancellation scenario, if any.
413	    fn cancel_violation(&self) -> Option<Violation> {
414	        let evidence = self.cancel.as_ref()?;
415	        if !evidence.fired {
416	            return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
417	                "the stream ended on its own before cancellation was fired, so this scenario \
418	                 tested no cancellation at all",
419	            ));
420	        }
421	        if !evidence.server_was_parked {
422	            return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
423	                "the server had already run its script to the end when the stream finished, so \
424	                 cancellation truncated nothing",
425	            ));
426	        }
427	        None
428	    }
429	}
430	
431	/// Drain one scenario's stream, cancelling part-way through when the scenario
432	/// calls for it.
433	///
434	/// For a cancellation scenario the sequence is: read every event the server
435	/// sent before the gate; wait for the stream to fall quiet, which is what
436	/// proves the server is withholding; fire the token; read whatever the driver
437	/// still emits; and only then release the gate — the release is what reports
438	/// whether the server really was parked on it.
439	///
440	/// The gate is deliberately *not* released before cancelling. Releasing first
441	/// would put the rest of the script on the wire in a race with the token, so a
442	/// correct driver could emit `Finish` from an already-delivered terminator
443	/// before it ever observed the cancellation, and the suite would report
444	/// `FinishOnCancel` against provider code that did nothing wrong.
445	async fn drain(
446	    mut stream: BoxStream<'static, Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>>,
447	    gate: Option<GateHandle>,
448	    scenario: Scenario,
449	    cancel: CancellationToken,
450	) -> Drained {
451	    let mut events = Vec::new();
452	
453	    if !is_cancel_scenario(scenario) {
454	        // Safety valve: a non-cancel scenario has nothing to synchronise on, so
455	        // an unreleased gate would stall the body until the timeout.
456	        if let Some(gate) = gate {
457	            gate.release();
458	        }
459	        while let Some(event) = stream.next().await {
460	            events.push(event);
461	        }
462	        return Drained {
463	            events,
464	            cancel: None,
465	        };
466	    }
467	
468	    let mut fired = false;
469	    loop {
470	        match tokio::time::timeout(GATE_QUIESCENCE, stream.next()).await {
471	            Ok(Some(event)) => events.push(event),
472	            // The stream ended by itself: the gate withheld nothing.
473	            Ok(None) => break,
474	            Err(_) => {
475	                // The stream has fallen silent, so the server is parked on the
476	                // gate. Fire the token while STILL HOLDING the gate. Do not
477	                // "simplify" this by releasing first: that puts the rest of the
478	                // script on the wire in a race with the token, so a correct
479	                // driver can emit `Finish` from an already-delivered terminator
480	                // before it ever observes the cancellation — and the suite would
481	                // report `FinishOnCancel` against provider code that did nothing
482	                // wrong, intermittently, depending on machine load. Holding is
483	                // also what makes the truncation provable further down.
484	                cancel.cancel();
485	                fired = true;
486	                break;
487	            }
488	        }
489	    }
490	
491	    if fired {
492	        while let Some(event) = stream.next().await {
493	            events.push(event);
494	        }
495	    }
496	
497	    let server_was_parked = gate.is_some_and(GateHandle::release);
498	    Drained {
499	        events,
500	        cancel: Some(CancelEvidence {
501	            fired,
502	            server_was_parked,
503	        }),
504	    }
505	}
506	
507	/// The positive-evidence floor for `scenario`, per spec §7.1.
508	///
509	/// Each floor asserts only the *vacuity* direction — too little evidence to
510	/// have tested anything. Excess is left to `classify`, which has a specific
511	/// name for it: two `Finish` events are a `DuplicateFinish`, and two
512	/// name-bearing deltas for one call are a `ToolNameNotExactlyOnce` (the exact
513	/// SMA-550 shape). A floor that also rejected the excess would mask both behind
514	/// `InsufficientEvidence`, which is the wrong diagnosis for a stream that
515	/// emitted too much.
516	///
517	/// The one exception is the `Err` count, because `classify` has no rule for a
518	/// stream that errors twice and would otherwise let it through unremarked.
519	///
520	/// The `FinishReason` check also lives here rather than in `classify`, and
521	/// must: `classify` has no fixture knowledge and its signature is fixed, while
522	/// the reason a `Finish` should carry is exactly a property of the bytes the
523	/// subject transcribed.
524	fn floor_violation(
525	    scenario: Scenario,
526	    events: &[Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>],
527	    tool_name: &str,
528	    finish_reason: Option<FinishReason>,
529	) -> Option<Violation> {
530	    match scenario {
531	        Scenario::CleanStop
532	        | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason
533	        | Scenario::TruncatedMidGeneration
534	        | Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration
535	        | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
536	        | Scenario::CancelMidGeneration
537	        | Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason => {
538	            if !events
539	                .iter()
540	                .any(|e| matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::TokenDelta { .. })))
541	            {
542	                return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
543	                    "no TokenDelta: a stream that emitted no text passes every ordering \
544	                     assertion vacuously",
545	                ));
546	            }
547	        }
548	        Scenario::FragmentedToolName
549	        | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
550	        | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop => {
551	            if !events
552	                .iter()
553	                .any(|e| matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { .. })))
554	            {
555	                return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
556	                    "no ToolCallDelta: a tool scenario that emitted no tool call passes \
557	                     assertion 7 vacuously",
558	                ));
559	            }
560	            if !events.iter().any(|e| {
561	                matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { name: Some(name), .. }) if name == tool_name)
562	            }) {
563	                return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
564	                    "no ToolCallDelta carried the tool name this subject declares, so the \
565	                     fixture served is not the one the scenario describes",
566	                ));
567	            }
568	        }
569	    }
570	
571	    // Assertion 8 checks every call-scoped `ProviderData` against the streamed
572	    // calls. With none in the stream it passes with no evidence, so this
573	    // scenario requires at least one.
574	    if matches!(scenario, Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop)
575	        && !events.iter().any(|e| {
576	            matches!(
577	                e,
578	                Ok(ModelEvent::ProviderData {
579	                    call_id: Some(_),
580	                    ..
581	                })
582	            )
583	        })
584	    {
585	        return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
586	            "no call-scoped ProviderData: assertion 8 would pass vacuously",
587	        ));
588	    }
589	
590	    // `CancelAfterStopReason` is the one degradation with no other detector.
591	    // `gate: None`, `fired` and `server_was_parked` all catch a cancellation
592	    // that withheld nothing, but none of them catches a gate placed one chunk
593	    // *too early* — withholding the stop-reason chunk and the usage chunk after
594	    // it. The stream then carries only `TokenDelta`s, quiesces, cancels, and
595	    // passes everything: the scenario silently ran `CancelMidGeneration` and
596	    // never exercised the case it exists for, a driver wrongly flushing a
597	    // *buffered* stop reason on cancel. The usage chunk is the fixture's own
598	    // marker for "the stop reason has gone past", so requiring it discriminates
599	    // a misplaced gate.
600	    //
601	    // Narrowing, recorded rather than implied: this is **vacuous for
602	    // anthropic**, whose `message_start` emits a `Usage` before any content
603	    // (`anthropic/stream.rs:71-85`), so the floor passes there no matter where
604	    // the gate sits. Anthropic's guarantee has to come from its fixture's
605	    // provenance comment instead — the transcription must show the gate sitting
606	    // after `message_delta`.
607	    //
608	    // Same narrowing applies to **gemini**, for the same shape of reason:
609	    // real Gemini traffic carries `usageMetadata` on every chunk, not only
610	    // the terminal one (see the `gemini` module's "`usageMetadata` appears
611	    // on every chunk" doc), so this floor is satisfied trivially there too —
612	    // its guarantee likewise rests on the gate placement documented at the
613	    // `CancelAfterStopReason` scenario site, not on this floor.
614	    if matches!(scenario, Scenario::CancelAfterStopReason)
615	        && !events
616	            .iter()
617	            .any(|e| matches!(e, Ok(ModelEvent::Usage { .. })))
618	    {
619	        return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(

619	        return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
620	            "no Usage: this scenario's script places a usage chunk after the stop-reason \
621	             chunk and gates on it, so a stream with no Usage was cancelled before the stop \
622	             reason was ever buffered — it ran CancelMidGeneration under another name",
623	        ));
624	    }
625	
626	    if matches!(
627	        scenario,
628	        Scenario::CleanStop
629	            | Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason
630	            | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
631	            | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
632	    ) {
633	        // The first `Finish` on purpose: a second one is a `DuplicateFinish`,
634	        // which `classify` names precisely, and checking the reason on the
635	        // first is what tells a wrong fixture from a wrong driver.
636	        let observed = events.iter().find_map(|event| match event {
637	            Ok(ModelEvent::Finish { reason }) => Some(reason.clone()),
638	            _ => None,
639	        });
640	        match observed {
641	            // Only the two *clean stop* scenarios floor the absence of a
642	            // `Finish`. For `TruncatedAfterStopReason` the absence is assertion
643	            // 3 — the SMA-531 shape — which `classify` reports as
644	            // `MissingFinish`; a floor here would mask the one bug class that
645	            // scenario exists to catch behind `InsufficientEvidence`.
646	            None if matches!(
647	                scenario,
648	                Scenario::CleanStop
649	                    | Scenario::ToolCallCleanStop
650	                    | Scenario::ThinkingToolCallCleanStop
651	            ) =>
652	            {
653	                return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
654	                    "no Finish: a clean stop that never terminated proves nothing about \
655	                     terminality",
656	                ));
657	            }
658	            None => {}
659	            Some(observed) => {
660	                let Some(expected) = finish_reason else {
661	                    return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
662	                        "this scenario must end with a Finish, but the subject declares no \
663	                         FinishReason for it, so its fixture is not the one the scenario \
664	                         describes",
665	                    ));
666	                };
667	                if observed != expected {
668	                    return Some(Violation::FinishReasonMismatch { expected, observed });
669	                }
670	            }
671	        }
672	    }
673	
674	    if matches!(
675	        scenario,
676	        Scenario::ErrorMidGeneration | Scenario::ErrorAfterStopReason
677	    ) && events.iter().filter(|e| e.is_err()).count() != 1
678	    {
679	        return Some(Violation::InsufficientEvidence(
680	            "an error scenario must yield exactly one Err: none means the aborted body was \
681	             read as a clean end-of-stream, more than one means the stream kept going after \
682	             it failed",
683	        ));
684	    }
685	
686	    None
687	}

689	/// Compare the declines this subject actually produced against [`DECLINED`],
690	/// and panic on any difference in either direction.
691	///
692	/// Both directions matter. An unexpected decline is the escape hatch this
693	/// pinning exists to close. An expected decline that stopped happening matters
694	/// just as much: the subject now serves that scenario, so the table is lying
695	/// about the provider — and the row would go on excusing a future regression
696	/// that reintroduced the decline.
697	fn assert_declines_match(subject: &str, observed: &[(Scenario, &'static str)]) {
698	    let expected: Vec<(Scenario, &'static str)> = DECLINED
699	        .iter()
700	        .filter(|(name, _, _)| *name == subject)
701	        .map(|(_, scenario, reason)| (*scenario, *reason))
702	        .collect();
703	
704	    let mut problems: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
705	
706	    for (scenario, reason) in observed {
707	        match expected.iter().find(|(s, _)| s == scenario) {
708	            None => problems.push(format!(
709	                "  unexpected decline of {scenario:?} ({reason:?}). Declining is for a wire \
710	                 shape that cannot physically occur — if that is the case here, add a \
711	                 reviewed row to DECLINED; otherwise serve the scenario."
712	            )),
713	            Some((_, pinned)) if pinned != reason => problems.push(format!(
714	                "  decline reason for {scenario:?} drifted: DECLINED says {pinned:?}, the \
715	                 subject said {reason:?}"
716	            )),
717	            Some(_) => {}
718	        }
719	    }
720	
721	    for (scenario, reason) in &expected {
722	        if !observed.iter().any(|(s, _)| s == scenario) {
723	            problems.push(format!(
724	                "  {scenario:?} is pinned as declined ({reason:?}) but the subject served it. \
725	                 The row is stale: remove it, so it cannot excuse a future regression."
726	            ));
727	        }
728	    }
729	
730	    assert!(
731	        problems.is_empty(),
732	        "conformance: {subject} — decline set does not match DECLINED (spec §6.2):\n{}",
733	        problems.join("\n")
734	    );
735	}
736	
737	/// Panic naming the subject, the scenario and the violation.
738	///
739	/// Tasks registering a new subject read these while transcribing fixtures, so
740	/// the message carries what to look at, not just what failed.
741	fn fail(subject: &str, scenario: Scenario, violation: &Violation, detail: &str) -> ! {
742	    panic!("conformance: {subject} / {scenario:?} — {violation:?}\n  {detail}");
743	}

745	/// A one-line summary of what a stream emitted, for failure output.
746	fn summarise(events: &[Result<ModelEvent, ModelError>]) -> String {
747	    if events.is_empty() {
748	        return "<nothing>".to_owned();
749	    }
750	    events
751	        .iter()
752	        .map(|event| match event {
753	            Ok(ModelEvent::TokenDelta { .. }) => "TokenDelta".to_owned(),
754	            Ok(ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta { .. }) => "ReasoningDelta".to_owned(),
755	            Ok(ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta { call_id, name, .. }) => match name {
756	                Some(name) => format!("ToolCallDelta({call_id}, name={name})"),
757	                None => format!("ToolCallDelta({call_id})"),
758	            },
759	            Ok(ModelEvent::Usage { .. }) => "Usage".to_owned(),
760	            Ok(ModelEvent::Finish { reason }) => format!("Finish({reason:?})"),
761	            Ok(other) => format!("{other:?}"),
762	            Err(err) => format!("Err({err:?})"),
763	        })
764	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
765	        .join(", ")
766	}

1	//! The registered conformance subjects.
2	//!
3	//! Each subject in this file serves its own wire bytes through the crate's
4	//! paced HTTP server and hands back the stream from its real `Model::invoke`,
5	//! so every assertion in `assert_conforms` is made about production driver and
6	//! production translator code — never about a reimplementation of either.
7	//!
8	//! ## Adding a subject
9	//!
10	//! One `mod <subject> { … }` per subject, holding its fixture helpers, its
11	//! `StreamUnderTest` impl and one `#[tokio::test]` that calls
12	//! `assert_conforms`. The module scoping is not cosmetic: it is what lets every
13	//! subject call its helpers `text_delta`, `script`, `request` and so on without
14	//! a per-subject prefix, and it keeps six subjects' worth of near-identical
15	//! names from colliding in one flat namespace.
16	//!
17	//! Two rules apply to every subject, and both exist because breaking them makes
18	//! a check pass without measuring anything:
19	//!
20	//! 1. **Decline reasons are literal strings**, copied by hand from
21	//!    `src/declines.rs`. A subject that looked its reasons up from `DECLINED`
22	//!    would satisfy that table's two-directional cross-check by construction,
23	//!    which is exactly the drift the table exists to catch.
24	//! 2. **`encodes_stop_reason` is measured from the bytes about to be served**,
25	//!    never restated from `Scenario::expects_stop_reason`. Restating it
26	//!    compares the harness's expectation with itself. See the Bedrock impl for
27	//!    what it catches.
28	//!
29	//! ## Key order
30	//!
31	//! Each wire helper that builds a JSON payload uses `json!` and serializes the
32	//! `serde_json::Value`. (The `done()` helpers are byte literals.) The
33	//! `serde_json` 1.0.154 in `Cargo.lock` has no `preserve_order` feature, so
34	//! the keys come out in alphabetical order. That order can differ from the
35	//! order in the cited sources. No translator depends on key order: each one
36	//! decodes the payload as a JSON object.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The spec's facts are correct. The cited line ranges, the fragment bytes, the translator lines and the harness behaviour all match the code, and no harness check rejects the new data. Two problems need a fix before implementation. First, the doc edit list misses two provenance statements that become false. Second, the spec claims that the suite checks a property it does not check, and its acceptance criteria only ask that the tests still pass.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
None.

### MAJOR
- **Two provenance statements become false, and step 6 does not list them** - The new constant cites all three captures. Two sentences in the module doc then become false. `conformance.rs:1667-1668` says: "Only one fixture that a helper copies is CAPTURED: `thinking_text_tool_use.txt`." `conformance.rs:1744-1748` says that `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt` and `redacted_thinking_tool_use.txt` are fixtures "that no helper in this module copies a shape from". `conformance.rs:1669-1671` ("the ... `tool_use` helpers copy HAND-AUTHORED shapes") is also only half true after the change, because the `input_json_delta` values now come from captures. | Why it matters: this suite treats provenance prose as load-bearing (SMA-845 existed only to make these labels true), and no gate checks prose. Two engineers can also build different things here. One can ground `CAPTURED_ARGS` on all three captures and edit these lines. The other can ground it on `thinking_text_tool_use.txt` only, cite the other two as having the same bytes, and leave these lines alone. | Suggested fix: decide which grounding to use and write the decision in the spec. Then add 1667-1671 and 1744-1748 to step 6, with the new meaning of each.

- **The spec claims that the suite checks a property it does not check, and no criterion shows that the new data catches anything** - The anti-goal says that the main property under test is that "the translator gives the name to the first `input_json_delta`, also when `partial_json` is empty". The harness does not check that. Assertion 7 (`check.rs:92-121`) counts the deltas that carry a name for each `call_id`. It does not check which delta carries the name. I traced three possible translator changes against the new script:
  (a) The translator puts the name on every delta: the count is 4, and `ToolNameNotExactlyOnce` fails. The old one-delta script cannot catch this.
  (b) The translator does not send the empty delta but still sets `name_emitted`: no delta carries the name. The floor at `lib.rs:560-567` ("no ToolCallDelta carried the tool name...") fails first, so assertion 7 never runs.
  (c) The translator drops empty deltas before the name logic: the name moves to `{"city"`, the count is 1, and the suite passes. The core contract (`core/src/model.rs:265-270`) permits this.
  All the goals (lines 27-33) are "still passes" conditions, and the current code meets them with or without the change. | Why it matters: the rewritten module doc will copy the overclaim into load-bearing text. Without a mutation check, nobody has shown that the change adds coverage. | Suggested fix: change the anti-goal to the true property: "exactly one delta carries the name, for a call with four deltas whose first delta is empty". Add an acceptance criterion: do mutations (a) and (b) on `stream.rs:175-185`, confirm that `anthropic::conforms` fails with the expected violation, and record the result in the PR. State that (c) passes on purpose.

### MINOR
- **Step 6 does not match the comment text, and the section title is referenced in three places** - Step 6 says the two script comments "lose 'one whole `input_json_delta`'". Only the `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` comment uses that phrase (`conformance.rs:2225-2226`). The `ToolCallCleanStop` comment (`2195-2201`) says "the whole argument JSON arrives on one `input_json_delta`". It also says "Matches `parallel_tool_use.txt`'s single-call shape", which becomes false for the delta part. The rename of the section heading (`1805`) also breaks three prose references to the old title: `1721`, `2067-2068` and `2198-2199` ("never splits" section). Rustdoc does not check these references. | Suggested fix: list each sentence to change by line, including the three title references.

- **The rewrite must drop or reword two parts of the old section** - `conformance.rs:1819-1822` ("The SMA-845 audit ... does not change this test data") becomes history after this change. `1823-1826` claims that one delta "fully exercises assertion 7's 'exactly one, not zero'". In fact the floor at `lib.rs:560-567` catches the "zero" case before `classify` runs. | Suggested fix: tell the builder to remove or reword 1819-1822, and to name the floor as the check for the "zero" case and assertion 7 as the check for "more than one".

- **"each SMA-840 capture" is ambiguous** - SMA-840 added five fixtures. The two HAND-AUTHORED ones split the arguments differently, into `{"city":` and `"Paris"}` (`interleaved_thinking.txt:54-60`, `unsigned_thinking_tool_use.txt:49-55`). | Suggested fix: in the constant doc, write "each of the three CAPTURED SMA-840 fixtures".

- **The request text change is not necessary, but it does no harm** - `PacedServer` records only the headers of the first request and never reads the body (`server.rs:191-194`). No check reads the user message, and `request()` is the only place in the module that uses it (`conformance.rs:2269`). The change keeps the exchange coherent and has no effect on any test. The request text is not served bytes, so the provenance rule does not apply to it. After the change, this module says Paris and the other five modules say Berlin. That is acceptable. | Suggested fix: write in step 4 that the change is for coherence only. Then a reviewer does not look for a provenance source for it.

- **The new scan entries cannot fail** - `serde_json` escapes each `"` in a string value as `\"`. So no `partial_json` value can make the bytes `"stop_reason":"` in a frame. The four new entries in `scan_finds_only_a_populated_stop_reason` are harmless but add no check. The array element type is `(&'static str, Vec<u8>)`. So four entries need either four literal lines (which repeat the constant) or an iterator `chain`. | Suggested fix: one entry is enough. Or keep the four entries for symmetry and say that this is the reason.

- **The acceptance criteria and the book/README decision are not complete** - The goals list only `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance`. | Suggested fix: add `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Write that no book or README edit is necessary: the change is test-only and the crate has `publish = false` (`tests/provider-stream-conformance/Cargo.toml:5`). CLAUDE.md asks for this decision in writing.

### QUESTIONS
- SMA-567: does its JSON-parse check join the `args_delta` values for each `call_id` in stream order? Does it skip, trim or reject an empty fragment? If it requires each fragment to be non-empty, it conflicts with the anti-goal that keeps the empty first delta. If it joins in order, the result is `{"city": "Paris"}`, which is valid JSON.
- If SMA-567 merges first, does the "Risk" section require a rebase and a full new run of the suite? A text-only conflict fix does not prove that the new check passes on the new data.

## What's good
- The cited facts are exact. `thinking_text_tool_use.txt:143-153`, `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt:94-104` and `redacted_thinking_tool_use.txt:95-105` each run from the first delta's `event:` line to the last delta's `data:` line. All three send `""`, `{\"city\"`, `: \"Pari`, `s\"}`, and these join to valid JSON. `stream.rs:165-185` gives the name to the first `input_json_delta` also when it is empty. `model.rs:150-153` yields every event without a filter. No harness check and no core contract rule (`core/src/model.rs:282-294`) rejects an empty `args_delta`.
- The spec found every data site that depends on Berlin (`conformance.rs:2206`, `2239`, `2269`, `2422`), and nothing else depends on it. No check counts events in the tool scripts (`gate_after` is `None` for both scripts). For the thinking scenario, assertion 8 still has evidence: `stop_block` emits the call-scoped `ToolUse` position when `name_emitted` is true (`stream.rs:281-292`), and the floor at `lib.rs:574-588` sees it. The SMA-317 fixture headers (`parallel_tool_use.txt:31-33`, `tool_use_then_continuation.txt:39-41`) describe the fixtures, not the suite, so they stay true.
- The anti-goal that keeps the empty first delta and forbids invented fragments is correct. Approach A is the only option where every served argument byte comes from a capture. Approach B would copy the shape but not the data.
